lesson.menu_desc: Dialogue: dinner with the American team, answering open questions in three moves -- 33 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- The Business Dinner
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Pedro Monaco | Lesson 21 -- The Business Dinner

listenings.text: Here is a mistake I see at almost every business dinner. Somebody asks an open question, like what do you think of the city, and the other person gives a one-word answer. Fine. Good. Interesting. And then the conversation dies, and everybody looks at the menu. The problem is not the language. It is the shape of the answer. So I teach my clients a simple shape in three moves. First, answer the question directly, in one sentence. Second, add one detail that only you could give: a reason, a small story, a number. This is where the emphasis lives. I do like the city, but the traffic is so bad that I listen to two audiobooks a week. Third, hand the question back. And what about you? That third move is the one most people forget, and it is the one that turns an interview into a conversation. Three moves, about thirty seconds. That is all it takes.

My first dinner with American clients was such a disaster that I still remember the name of the restaurant. I had prepared for the meeting for two weeks. I knew every clause of the contract. But nobody at the table wanted to talk about the contract. They asked me about football, about the city, about my weekend. And I answered every question with three words. Yes, it's nice. No, not really. The silences were so long that one of them started checking his phone. On the way back to the hotel, my boss gave me some advice I have never forgotten. She said: they did respect your work today. Now they want to know if they like you. After that, I started preparing for dinners the way I prepare for meetings. I think of three stories I can tell and two questions I can ask. It does feel strange to prepare small talk, but it works.

extra_audio.text: First, Megan asks if they can talk about something other than contracts. Then she asks Pedro whether he likes living in São Paulo. Next, Pedro answers, adds a detail about the traffic and asks her a question back. After that, Megan asks him why he chose law. Finally, she tells him he is the first person today who has really opened up.
